newsitem.title: USA: US asks for WTO consultations on Brazil car rules.
newsitem.headline: US asks for WTO consultations on Brazil car rules.

text.p: The United States formally asked the World Trade Organization on Friday for consultations with Brazil on its rules limiting car imports, the U.S. Trade Representative's Office said.

A spokesman for the USTR said the United States wanted to discuss Brazil's preferential treatment of car imports from Japan, South Korea and the European Union, which had complained about Brazil's high tariffs on car imports.
The United States also wants to discuss concerns about a Brazilian program launched in December to attract car manufacturing investment in its poor northeast district, the spokesman said.
Under Brazil's car regime, manufacturers based in that South American country can import vehicles at 35 percent tariff. Competitors without manufacturing in Brazil face a hefty 70-percent duty.
The aim of the program was to spur investment in local production. Car companies have pledged to invest at least $17 billion by the end of the decade.
Japan, South Korea, and the EU had filed complaints with the WTO, prompting Brazil to initiate a program allowing some imports from those countries to be imported at the lower tariff.

The spokesman said the United States had delayed action based on a Brazilian commitment to discuss U.S. objections, but that a U.S. proposal for resolution had been rejected and no counterproposal made.

The request for WTO consultations was made under a Section 301 trade law investigation initiated on October 11, 1996, the spokesman said. A request for consultations is the first step in a WTO dispute settlement case.
